question: A 59-year-old woman with a past medical history of atrial fibrillation currently on warfarin presents to the emergency department for acute onset dizziness. She was watching TV in the living room when she suddenly felt the room spin around her as she was getting up to go to the bathroom. She denies any fever, weight loss, chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, lightheadedness, or pain but reports difficulty walking and hiccups. A physical examination is significant for rotary nystagmus and decreased pin prick sensation throughout her left side. A magnetic resonance image (MRI) of the head is obtained and shows ischemic changes of the right lateral medulla. What other symptoms would you expect to find in this patient?

options.opd: Paralysis of the right lower limb

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Ischemic changes of the right lateral medulla -> lateral medullary syndrome -> Wallenberg syndrome -> neurologic deficits involving the brainstem -> 80% CHAIN: Ischemic changes of the right lateral medulla -> disruption of the vestibular nuclei -> vertigo -> 70% CHAIN: Ischemic changes of the right lateral medulla -> involvement of the nucleus ambiguus -> dysphagia -> decreased gag reflex -> 75% CHAIN: Ischemic changes of the right lateral medulla -> involvement of the hypoglossal nucleus -> tongue deviation to the left side -> left-sided tongue deviation -> 70% CHAIN: Ischemic changes of the right lateral medulla -> involvement of the corticospinal tract -> paralysis of the right lower limb -> paralysis of the right lower limb -> 80% CHAIN: Ischemic changes of the right lateral medulla -> involvement of the facial nerve nucleus -> right-sided facial paralysis -> right-sided facial paralysis -> 80%
analysis: Based on the clinical presentation of acute onset dizziness, rotary nystagmus, difficulty walking, hiccups, and decreased pin prick sensation on the left side along with MRI findings of right lateral medullary ischemia, the patient is likely experiencing a lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome. This syndrome typically involves a constellation of symptoms due to the involvement of various structures in the medulla.
